title: Tor-independent stalk comparison for a perfect pullback
statement: Let f:X\to S and g:S'\to S be morphisms of schemes and form the cartesian square X'=X\times_S S' with projections g_X:X'\to X and f':X'\to S' [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change]. Assume f and g are Tor independent in the stalkwise sense: for every x\in X and s'\in S' over the same s\in S, \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathcal O_{S,s}}(\mathcal O_{X,x},\mathcal O_{S',s'})=0 for i>0. If P is a perfect complex on X [def-pc-perfect-complex], then for every x'\in X' with x=g_X(x'), s'=f'(x') and s=f(x), and every i\in\mathbf Z, the canonical map $$H^i(P_x\mathbin{\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}}\mathcal O_{S',s'})\mathbin{\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'}}}\mathcal O_{X',x'}\longrightarrow H^i\bigl((Lg_X^*P)_{x'}\bigr)$$ is an isomorphism [def-pc-derived-pullback].

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: local affine reduction and the Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: Fix x' and write R=\mathcal O_{S,s}, A=\mathcal O_{X,x}, B=\mathcal O_{S',s'}, and C=\mathcal O_{X',x'}. Choose affine neighbourhoods of x and s' and use the affine perfect-model criterion [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] after localizing at x; thus P_x is represented by a bounded complex Q^\bullet of finite projective A-modules.

The assumed stalkwise Tor-independence is Tor_i^R(A,B)=0 for i>0. Apply [lem-pc-tor-independent-projective-complex-tensor] to Q^\bullet, with E=A\otimes_R B and D=C. It gives the required cohomology isomorphism after identifying Q^\bullet\otimes_A D with the pulled-back stalk complex.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: Choose the affine open U=\operatorname{Spec}(A_0)\ni x of Step 1 with P|_U\cong\widetilde{P_0^\bullet}, P_0^\bullet a bounded complex of finite projective A_0-modules, so that Q^\bullet=P_0^\bullet\otimes_{A_0}A. By [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde](1), (Lg_X^*P)|_{g_X^{-1}U}\cong L(g_X|_{g_X^{-1}U})^*\widetilde{P_0^\bullet}. Each \widetilde{P_0^n} is a direct summand of a finite free \mathcal O_U-module, hence flat, so by [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback] this derived pullback is represented by the termwise pullback g_X^*\widetilde{P_0^\bullet}. Apply the stalk pullback identification [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] degreewise; its naturality identifies (g_X^*\widetilde{P_0^\bullet})_{x'} with Q^\bullet\otimes_A C, hence (Lg_X^*P)_{x'}\cong Q^\bullet\otimes_A C. The canonical map A\otimes_R B\to C is a localization (on affine opens \operatorname{Spec}A_0, \operatorname{Spec}B_0 over \operatorname{Spec}R_0 the local ring C is a localization of A_0\otimes_{R_0}B_0, of which A\otimes_R B is itself a localization, by the affine description of fibre products, Stacks, Schemes, Section on fibre products), so tensoring with C is exact [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] and commutes with cohomology. Under these identifications the isomorphism of Step 2 is exactly the displayed canonical map, for every i.
